A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from GSTAR to GauSTAR. All 10 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v3 are readable and support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or the separately referenced supplementary material.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 report original appearance, geometry, and AprilTag tracking experiments, including baseline comparisons in Table 1 and component ablations in Table 2.

after.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the original reconstruction, tracking, and ablation results in Tables 1–2, with qualitative demonstrations in Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain Gaussian binding, scene-flow initialization, fixed-topology optimization, adaptive unbinding and duplication, and surface re-meshing. Added wording about pixel coordinates and merging matched vertices clarifies the existing procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same captured reconstruction and AprilTag tracking sequences and retain the human, object-interaction, and robot examples. The new pointer to public-dataset code information does not document additional evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains HumanRF, Dynamic 3D Gaussians, PhysAvatar-general, PhysAvatar-SMPLX, and 2D Gaussian Splatting. Figures 4–5 retain their corresponding comparator subsets. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain unchanged: four appearance sequences totaling 850 frames, five test views, and two tracking sequences with six AprilTags and five points per tag. Acquisition settings, evaluation metrics, and the control using HumanRF depth instead of IR depth are retained.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same unbinding, re-meshing, and scene-flow ablations. The without-IR comparison and application demonstrations also remain. The added transparent/specular-surface limitation is not accompanied by a new robustness experiment or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Tables 1–2 retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains the proposed method's PSNR of 31.87, Chamfer Distance of 0.237 cm, and 3D ATE of 0.452 cm. Figures 4–6 retain the same qualitative examples and findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and their mathematical definitions remain unchanged, including Gaussian parameterization, flow smoothing, reconstruction regularizers, and unbinding weights and loss. Wording and punctuation edits introduce no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about appearance reconstruction, surface reconstruction, and tracking under topology changes. The claim of matching or surpassing comparison methods is retained; the method rename does not change its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds transparent and specular surfaces as a limitation and future-work topic, while removing the caveat about substantial Gaussian/mesh optimization resources and its real-time-rendering tradeoff. Existing topology-change and multi-view limitations remain. Section 4.3 also changes scene flow 'prevents' trapping in local minima to 'helps prevent'.

D1.justification: The project/code link changes to ETH AIT's GauSTAR page. Section 4.1 newly points to supplementary code-release information for public datasets, and the added acknowledgements disclose use of the ETH Zurich Euler cluster. These are access-information and compute disclosures; the referenced releases themselves are outside the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to TAP-Vid, OcclusionFusion, DTexFusion, and A Self-Occlusion Aware Lighting Model for Real-Time Dynamic Reconstruction. All 51 earlier references are retained. This modestly expands background attribution without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: GSTAR becomes GauSTAR throughout. Localized copyediting clarifies Gaussian definitions, flow projection, and vertex merging, and an acknowledgements section is added. The main section order and narrative organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and both tables are retained. Figure 5 adds a pale green grouping around the input frames and adjusts spacing. Method labels and some captions change, while acknowledgements and expanded references cause limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves explanatory precision in Sections 3.2 and 3.5, qualifies the claim about avoiding local minima, and adds a concrete material limitation. Background attribution also improves. Removing the optimization-cost caveat loses some practical transparency, but the clarification gains support a small overall improvement. The method and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
